title: Treble cluster hexagon
subtitle: A bold raised corner at each of the six points — the cluster stands out clearly in a single colour
excerpt: The treble cluster hexagon replaces the open chain-2 corner construction with a full 5-treble cluster at each of the six corners, giving a more defined point that reads clearly even in a single colour. Four rounds give a 12 cm point-to-point motif with a noticeably different silhouette from the standard hexagon.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1-3 (1885-1890) — cluster and raised-point hexagonal motifs (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet motif chapter.
heroPrompt: A treble cluster crochet hexagon in deep teal DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight — the 12 cm motif has six bold raised cluster points visible from across the room.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished four-round treble cluster hexagon measures 12 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking.

chartDefinition.title: Treble cluster hexagon
chartDefinition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. A 5-tr treble cluster sits at each of the six corners on every round, replacing the open ch-2 corner of the standard hexagon. Chain-1 side spaces separate the cluster groups between corners.

glossaryTerms.definition: Multiple trebles worked into the same stitch or space with their final loops joined together at the top, giving a gathered point. A 5-tr cluster draws five trebles together into one raised tip.
The gap created by skipping a chain or chains. In the treble cluster hexagon, a chain-2 space sits at the base of each 5-tr cluster corner; chain-1 spaces separate side groups.

content.text: The treble cluster hexagon puts a raised
treble-cluster

of five trebles at each of the six corner points instead of the open (3tr, ch 2, 3tr) group used in the standard hexagon. The gathered tips stand proud of the surface on the right side, making the six corners more defined — the motif reads clearly even in a single colour and from a distance.
Between the six corner clusters, the side spaces use the standard three-treble
chain-space

construction familiar from granny squares and the basic hexagon. The main technique to practise before starting is the 5-treble cluster: work five trebles into the same space, stopping before the final pull-through of each one, then draw yarn through all six loops on the hook at once.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK-weight cotton in one to three colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished four-round treble cluster hexagon measures 12 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after steam-blocking. Make a test motif before starting a large project — the cluster tips can pull tighter than standard clusters and affect the overall diameter.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
5-tr cluster (5tr-cl) — five trebles worked into the same space, loops joined at the top. UK; the same technique as US 5-dc cluster.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern

Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. The 5-tr cluster counts as one corner unit. Ch 3 at the start of each round does NOT count as a treble here — it lifts the yarn to the correct height before the first cluster. Do not turn.
Round 1

Form a magic ring. Ch 3 (does not count as st). Work a 5-tr cluster into the ring: [yarn over, insert hook into ring, pull up loop, yarn over, pull through 2 loops] 5 times into the ring, then yarn over and pull through all 6 loops on hook. *Ch 2, work a 5-tr cluster into the ring*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of first cluster to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 cluster points, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 2

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Work a 5-tr cluster into the same sp. *Ch 2, into same sp work a second 5-tr cluster. Ch 1. Into next ch-2 sp work a 5-tr cluster*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, into same sp work a second 5-tr cluster. Ch 1. Sl st to top of first cluster to join. (12 clusters, 6 ch-2 spaces, 6 ch-1 side spaces.)
Round 3

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Work a 5-tr cluster into same sp. Ch 2, work a second 5-tr cluster into same sp. Ch 1. *Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (5-tr cluster, ch 2, 5-tr cluster). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1. Sl st to top of first cluster to join. (12 corner clusters, 6 side clusters, 6 ch-2 corners, 12 ch-1 side spaces.)
Round 4

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Work a 5-tr cluster into same sp. Ch 2, work a second 5-tr cluster into same sp. Ch 1. *[Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1.] twice. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (5-tr cluster, ch 2, 5-tr cluster). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. [Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1.] twice. Sl st to top of first cluster to join. Fasten off. (12 corner clusters, 12 side clusters, 6 ch-2 corners, 18 ch-1 side spaces.)
Chart
The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Corner cluster pairs sit at all six points on every round; standard three-treble side clusters fill the edges from round 3.

definition.title: Treble cluster hexagon
definition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. 5-tr clusters mark all six corners throughout. Standard 3-tr clusters fill the side spaces from round 3. Chain-1 spaces between all groups.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Thread through a tapestry needle and weave through 3 to 4 stitches on the wrong side, reverse direction through 2 to 3 stitches, and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail. Steam-block on a foam mat with all six cluster points pinned — the raised tips benefit from gentle pinning to hold their shape while the yarn relaxes.
Joining

Join along each of the six sides through the back loops of the side cluster groups and through the ch-2 spaces at the corner tips. The raised cluster tips sit slightly proud of the seam after joining — this is correct; the tip reading as a defined point is part of the motif's character.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a delicates cycle. The cluster tips may compress in the wash — re-pin them while damp to restore the shape. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

The popcorn hexagon uses a different raised stitch at each corner point — a popcorn rather than a cluster, giving an even more prominent raised dot. The lacy hexagon moves in the opposite direction: open chain-3 side spaces instead of solid clusters, for an airy finish.
